checklist.step: Build the annual retention inventory
actions: Pull the ACA/PHSA filing calendar for the plan year from the compliance evidence repository and list every SERFF, NAIC iSite+/eFiling, and CMS MLR/MCAS submission due.
Open a retention inventory workbook in Microsoft Excel with columns for filing type, system of record, submission date, and owning team.
Circulate the draft to the Regulatory Filing Specialist and Regulatory Reporting Analyst for confirmation of scope.
Lock the inventory once both teams confirm no filings are missing.
checklist.done: the inventory lists every due submission with owner and target date confirmed by both filing teams.

checklist.step: Capture each SERFF filing package at submission
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access, locate the tracking number handed off by the Regulatory Filing Specialist.
Export the full submission package — forms, rate exhibits, correspondence, disposition letter — as PDF.
Save it into the document management repository under <state>-<TOI>-<tracking number>.
Cross-check the disposition date and status shown on the export against the retention inventory row.
checklist.done: every SERFF filing in the inventory has an exported package filed under its tracking number.

checklist.step: Capture NAIC statutory statement submissions
actions: In NAIC iSite+/eFiling open the Annual Statement or Quarterly Statement filing history for the company code.
Download the submitted blank, jurat page, and NAIC submission confirmation.
Save alongside the Controller's filed-statement package in the financial reporting repository.
Log the NAIC confirmation number on the retention inventory row.
checklist.done: each statutory statement submission is archived with its jurat page and confirmation number.

checklist.step: Capture the ACA MLR annual report and CMS confirmation
actions: Request the submitted MLR reporting form and the CMS acknowledgement/confirmation receipt from the Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
Save into the archive under the reporting year and state/market.
Confirm the premium, claims, and quality-improvement figures on the archived form match the version actually transmitted to CMS.
checklist.done: the filed MLR form and CMS confirmation are archived and match the transmitted version.

checklist.step: Capture the MCAS submission and NAIC confirmation
actions: Obtain the MCAS submission export and NAIC confirmation receipt from the Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
File under the reporting year in the archive.
Verify the confirmation lists the correct number of data elements submitted for the Individual Health line.
checklist.done: the MCAS submission package and confirmation are archived and element counts reconcile.

checklist.step: Capture CSR plan-variation filings and supporting actuarial memoranda
actions: Pull the approved CSR (73/87/94) plan-variation filings and their actuarial memoranda from the Product Filing Specialist and Appointed Actuary.
File each with its parent QHP filing in the archive.
Note the SERFF tracking number of each variant against its parent QHP tracking number.
checklist.done: every CSR variant filing is archived and cross-referenced to its parent QHP tracking number.

checklist.step: Classify and label each archived record by retention category
actions: Apply the retention schedule code (10-year statutory, permanent regulatory, or audit-cycle) to each folder in the document management repository.
Tag each record by type — filing package, statement, MLR, MCAS, CSR memorandum.
Confirm the labels match the company retention schedule table.
checklist.done: every archived record carries a retention label consistent with the retention schedule.

checklist.step: Index each record for retrieval
actions: Enter state, TOI/form number, tracking or confirmation number, and filing date into the archive index.
Confirm the record is searchable by any of those fields.
Spot-check three random entries by searching the index and opening the record.
checklist.done: the three spot-checked entries are found and open correctly by index search.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to the retention inventory
actions: Compare the inventory workbook line-by-line to the archive index.
List any inventory row without a matching archived record.
Hand the gap list to step 10 for chase-down.
checklist.done: every inventory row has a matching archived record or is listed as an open gap.

checklist.step: Chase and close open gaps
actions: For each unmatched row, request the missing package from the originating team — Regulatory Filing Specialist, Regulatory Reporting Analyst, or Appointed Actuary — with a 5-business-day due date.
Escalate to the Compliance Officer if unresolved after 10 business days.
Log the resolution date and archive location once the gap is closed.
checklist.done: every gap is closed or escalated with an owner and date.

checklist.step: Apply legal hold flags where an exam or litigation is pending
actions: Check with Regulatory Counsel for any open market conduct exam, MLR audit, or litigation touching the Individual Health block.
Flag the affected records as legal hold in the repository to suspend the retention clock.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel that the hold list is current each quarter.
checklist.done: all records relevant to an open exam or litigation are flagged legal hold.

checklist.step: Restrict access to sensitive submission detail
actions: Confirm repository folder permissions limit edit rights to Records Management and read rights to Compliance, Regulatory Reporting and Legal.
Remove any standing access for departed staff.
Log the permission review date.
checklist.done: folder permissions match the approved access list.

checklist.step: Run a quarterly archive integrity spot-check
actions: Select five records at random each quarter.
Retrieve and confirm the content is complete, unaltered, and matches its retention label.
Log results in the quarterly integrity log.
checklist.done: the quarterly spot-check log shows five records checked with no unresolved discrepancies.

checklist.step: Certify completeness by September 30
actions: Total the year's inventory count against the archived count.
Prepare a completeness certification memo listing any residual open gaps.
Obtain sign-off on the memo.
checklist.done: a signed completeness certification is dated on or before September 30.

checklist.step: Report retention status to the Compliance Officer
actions: Summarize inventory counts, open gaps, and certification status.
Present the summary at the next compliance committee meeting.
File the summary in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the retention status summary is delivered to the Compliance Officer and filed.

testing.step: Build the test population of submissions filed in the period
actions: Extract SERFF Filing Access history, NAIC iSite+ submission history, and CMS MLR/MCAS confirmations for the test period.
Reconcile counts to the retention inventory maintained by Records Management.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the retention inventory and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the archive index
actions: Match each population row to an archived record by tracking or confirmation number.
List unmatched rows as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Record the match rate in the workpaper before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every population row is matched to an archived record or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of CSR-variant and MLR-related archive records.
Take a random, seeded sample of 15 additional records across SERFF and statutory statement filings, minimum 25 total.
Record the seed, population size, and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the retrieval for each sampled record
actions: Search the archive index using the tracking or confirmation number.
Open the archived package and confirm it is complete, legible, and unaltered against the source system (SERFF, NAIC iSite+, or CMS).
Note any discrepancy in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled record retrieves correctly and matches its source system.

testing.step: Verify retention labels and indexing on the sample
actions: Confirm each sampled record carries the correct retention label under the retention schedule.
Confirm each record is indexed on state, form/tracking number, and filing date.
Flag mislabeled or unindexed records.
testing.done: labeling and indexing on the sample match the retention schedule.

testing.step: Test access controls and legal holds
actions: Pull the repository permission report for the sampled folders.
Confirm access matches the approved list from Records Management.
Confirm any record tied to a known open exam or litigation carries a legal hold flag.
testing.done: access and legal-hold flags on the sample match expectations, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Recompute the retention-period math
actions: For each sampled record, recompute the retention expiry date from the filing or statement period end date and the applicable retention years.
Compare the recomputed date to the label applied.
Flag mismatches.
testing.done: recomputed retention dates match applied labels or are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Confirm the annual completeness certification agrees with source counts
actions: Recompute the year's inventory-to-archive count directly from the source systems.
Compare to the September 30 certification memo.
Investigate any variance with Records Management.
testing.done: certification counts tie to the recomputed source-system totals.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner, and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the record identifier and the gap found.
Assign a root cause (missed capture, wrong label, stale index) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next test cycle.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign, and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 100%-completeness threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the compliance committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Close the general ledger for the statutory period
actions: In the ERP general ledger module run the period-end close checklist and post final adjusting journal entries for the Individual Health legal entities.
Reconcile subledgers (premium, claims, reinsurance) to the GL trial balance in BlackLine (Close).
Lock the period once all reconciliations show a zero unexplained variance.
Export the final trial balance to the statutory close workbook.
checklist.done: the GL period is locked with all subledgers reconciled to a zero unexplained variance.

checklist.step: Pull the ACA Individual Health block trial balance segregated by legal entity and state
actions: Filter the locked trial balance to the Individual Health product/business unit codes.
Split premium, claims, and expense lines by writing company (NAIC co-code) and state of issue.
Reconcile the state split totals to the premium and claims registers maintained by Regulatory Reporting.
checklist.done: the trial balance is split by legal entity and state and reconciles to the underlying registers.

checklist.step: Prepare Schedule H — Accident and Health Exhibit
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) statement software open the Health Annual/Quarterly Statement blank and select Schedule H.
Populate premium earned, incurred claims, and reserve lines from the segregated trial balance.
Cross-check the EHB and lifetime/annual-limit-related disclosure lines against the product's benefit design to confirm no prohibited limits are reflected.
Flag any variance greater than 2% from the prior period for explanation.
checklist.done: Schedule H is populated, EHB/limit disclosures are confirmed clean, and variances over 2% are explained.

checklist.step: Prepare the Supplemental Health Care Exhibit (SHCE) Parts 1-3
actions: Populate SHCE Part 1 (Individual/Small Group/Large Group revenue and expense) using the state-segregated trial balance.
Populate SHCE Part 2 (federal/state taxes and MLR-eligible quality-improvement expense) and Part 3 (reconciliation to the audited statutory statement).
Reconcile SHCE premium and claims totals to the draft ACA MLR annual report figures from Regulatory Reporting.
Document and clear any tie-out break before proceeding.
checklist.done: SHCE Parts 1-3 are complete and reconcile to the draft MLR figures with no unresolved breaks.

checklist.step: Obtain claim reserve estimates from the Appointed Actuary
actions: Request the statutory claim reserve estimate (case reserves plus IBNR) for the Individual Health block from the Reserving Actuary.
Confirm the estimate is signed off by the Appointed Actuary and dated within the close cycle.
Post the reserve figure to Schedule H and the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
File the actuarial support memo with the close workpapers.
checklist.done: the actuarial reserve estimate is posted to the statement and its support memo is filed.

checklist.step: Prepare the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit statutory pages
actions: Populate the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit Statement of Income and Statement of Revenue and Expenses pages from the trial balance.
Tie total premiums written and net income to the GL and to Schedule H.
Reconcile investment income to the investment accounting subledger.
checklist.done: the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit ties to the GL, Schedule H, and investment subledger.

checklist.step: Compute Risk-Based Capital (RBC) inputs for the health block
actions: Extract the health underwriting risk, credit risk, and reserve risk inputs required by the health RBC formula.
Populate the RBC worksheet with the current-period statement figures.
Compare the resulting RBC ratio to the prior period and flag any material movement for CFO review.
checklist.done: the RBC worksheet is populated and any material ratio movement is flagged for CFO review.

checklist.step: Reconcile the statutory surplus roll-forward
actions: Roll forward beginning surplus plus net income, unrealized gains/losses, and capital contributions to the ending surplus figure.
Tie the ending surplus to the balance sheet page of the statement blank.
Document any reconciling item over $50,000.
checklist.done: the surplus roll-forward ties to the balance sheet with all items over $50,000 documented.

checklist.step: Load figures into the NAIC statement filing software
actions: In the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) software import or key the final Schedule H, SHCE, Underwriting and Investment Exhibit, and RBC figures.
Run the built-in cross-check/validation tool and clear all flagged edit errors.
Save a draft PDF of the complete blank for internal review.
checklist.done: the statement software validation runs clean with all edit errors cleared and a draft blank is produced.

checklist.step: Perform tie-out between SHCE, the draft MLR report, and Schedule H
actions: Line up SHCE premium/claims/expense totals against the corresponding draft MLR annual report figures.
Line up Schedule H incurred claims against the SHCE and MLR draft.
Investigate and document any variance greater than $10,000 before sign-off.
checklist.done: SHCE, the MLR draft, and Schedule H tie out, or every variance over $10,000 is documented.

checklist.step: Internal review by the Statutory Reporting Manager
actions: Review the draft blank against the prior-period filed statement for reasonableness.
Confirm every schedule referenced by the Health Annual Statement Instructions checklist is present and populated.
Note review comments in the close workbook and route back to preparer for any correction.
checklist.done: the review checklist is complete with all comments cleared.

checklist.step: CFO/Controller sign-off review meeting
actions: Walk through the draft blank, RBC ratio, and any flagged variances with the Controller.
Confirm the actuarial reserve figure and audit-open-item status before approving.
Record the sign-off decision and date in the close workbook.
checklist.done: the CFO sign-off is recorded with date in the close workbook.

checklist.step: Address auditor/actuary open items before lock
actions: Pull any open prior-period audit or actuarial review comments affecting the current statement.
Resolve or formally note each open item's disposition in the workpapers.
Obtain Appointed Actuary confirmation that reserve-related open items are cleared.
checklist.done: every open audit/actuarial item is resolved or its disposition is documented and actuary-confirmed.

checklist.step: Lock the statement package and generate the jurat page
actions: Generate the jurat page in the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) software listing the signing officers.
Route the jurat for the required officer signatures.
Lock the final statement package once signatures are complete.
checklist.done: the jurat page is signed and the statement package is locked.

checklist.step: Archive the finalized package
actions: Save the locked statement blank, SHCE, RBC worksheet, and tie-out workpapers into the financial reporting repository under the period.
Confirm ACA-specific supplemental certifications are finalized by September 30 ahead of the audited-statement cycle.
Notify Regulatory Reporting that the package is ready for filing.
checklist.done: the finalized package is archived and Regulatory Reporting is notified for filing.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory schedules and exhibits prepared in the period
actions: Extract the list of statement schedules and exhibits prepared for the Individual Health block, by writing company and state, from the close workbook.
Reconcile the extract to the statutory close calendar for the period.
Resolve any missing schedule before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the close calendar and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the GL trial balance to the filed statement
actions: Pull the locked GL trial balance for the period directly from the ERP.
Compare premium, claims, and expense totals to the corresponding lines on the filed statement blank.
List any variance as an automatic exception.
testing.done: GL totals tie to the filed statement, or every variance is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of Schedule H and SHCE line items.
Take a random, seeded sample of 10 additional supporting workpapers (RBC inputs, surplus roll-forward, subledger reconciliations).
Record the seed, population size, and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the SHCE-to-MLR and Schedule H tie-out
actions: Independently recompute the SHCE Part 1-3 totals from the underlying trial balance.
Compare to the filed SHCE and the draft MLR report figures.
Compare filed Schedule H incurred claims to the recomputed SHCE and MLR figures.
Log any difference as an exception.
testing.done: the independent tie-out matches the filed figures, or every difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace the reserve figure to the Appointed Actuary's support
actions: Pull the actuarial reserve support memo referenced in the close workpapers.
Confirm the Schedule H reserve line matches the actuary's signed figure and date.
Confirm the Appointed Actuary's sign-off pre-dates the statement lock date.
testing.done: the reserve figure traces to a dated, signed actuarial support memo pre-dating the lock date.

testing.step: Recompute the RBC ratio and surplus roll-forward
actions: Independently recompute the health RBC ratio from the filed statement inputs.
Recompute the surplus roll-forward from beginning surplus, net income, and other adjustments to the filed ending surplus.
Compare both to the filed figures and flag any mismatch.
testing.done: recomputed RBC ratio and surplus roll-forward match the filed statement, or mismatches are logged.

testing.step: Test the EHB/CSR-related disclosure lines for accuracy
actions: Review Schedule H disclosure lines against 45 CFR 156.410/156.420 and 45 CFR 156.130 to confirm no prohibited annual/lifetime limits are reflected.
Confirm CSR variant claim costs are reported under the correct SHCE reporting category.
Flag any misclassification for correction before the next filing.
testing.done: EHB/CSR-related disclosure lines are confirmed compliant, or misclassifications are flagged.

testing.step: Confirm the statement filed matches the locked, jurat-signed package
actions: Pull the locked package from the financial reporting repository.
Compare it page-by-page to the version actually submitted through Statutory Reporting (NAIC).
Confirm officer signatures on the jurat match the company's authorized signer list.
testing.done: the filed statement matches the locked package and jurat signatures are validated.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner, and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the schedule, line, and variance amount.
Assign a root cause (mapping error, late actuarial input, formula error) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next close cycle's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign, and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance tie-out threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the statement package is locked and jurat-signed before transmission
actions: Pull the locked, jurat-signed statement package from the financial reporting repository.
Confirm the Controller sign-off date and officer signatures are present.
Verify no open validation errors remain in the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) software.
checklist.done: the statement package is confirmed locked, signed, and validation-clean before transmission begins.

checklist.step: Transmit the statutory statement to the NAIC
actions: In NAIC iSite+/eFiling select the correct company code, filing period, and blank type (Quarterly or Annual).
Upload the final statement file and submit through the electronic filing gateway.
Capture the NAIC submission confirmation number and timestamp immediately on submission.
Save the confirmation to the transmittal log.
checklist.done: the statement is transmitted with a captured NAIC confirmation number and timestamp.

checklist.step: File the statutory statement with each required state insurance department
actions: Check each domiciliary and commercially-domiciled state's specific filing requirement (NAIC-only vs. direct state submission).
Submit directly to any state requiring a separate copy, via that state's portal or designated email address.
Log each state's acknowledgment or receipt confirmation on the transmittal log.
checklist.done: every state requiring a direct submission has a logged acknowledgment or receipt.

checklist.step: Prepare and validate the ACA MLR annual report file
actions: Pull the finalized premium, claims, quality-improvement, and tax data elements from the SHCE-reconciled MLR workbook.
Load the data into the CMS-prescribed MLR reporting form template.
Run the file through the CMS MLR reporting system's validation check and clear all flagged errors.
checklist.done: the MLR report file passes CMS validation with all flagged errors cleared.

checklist.step: Submit the ACA MLR annual report to CMS by July 31
actions: Log in to the CMS MLR reporting system and select the correct issuer and reporting year.
Upload the validated MLR report file for each State and market.
Capture the CMS confirmation receipt with submission date and time.
File the confirmation in the transmittal log before the July 31 deadline.
checklist.done: the MLR report is submitted for every State/market with a CMS confirmation captured before July 31.

checklist.step: Reconcile submitted figures back to the filed statutory statement
actions: Compare the transmitted MLR report premium and claims totals to the filed SHCE and Schedule H.
Compare the transmitted statutory statement totals to the Controller's locked package.
Document and escalate any post-transmission variance immediately.
checklist.done: transmitted figures reconcile to the filed source documents with no unresolved variance.

checklist.step: Monitor for rejection or deficiency notices
actions: Check NAIC iSite+/eFiling and the CMS MLR system daily for 5 business days after each submission for rejection or deficiency notices.
Log any notice received with its stated defect.
Route deficiency notices to the Controller and Regulatory Reporting Manager same-day.
checklist.done: the 5-business-day monitoring window is completed with any notice logged and routed same-day.

checklist.step: Correct and refile any rejected submission
actions: Diagnose the rejection reason against the validation error or deficiency notice.
Correct the underlying data with the Controller and resubmit through the same filing system.
Confirm the resubmission receives a clean acceptance confirmation within 2 business days of the original rejection.
checklist.done: every rejected submission is corrected and re-accepted within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Update the filing calendar with actual submission and confirmation dates
actions: Enter the actual submission date, confirmation number, and acceptance status for each filing into the filing calendar/tracker.
Flag any submission filed within 2 business days of its statutory deadline for root-cause review.
Attach the confirmation document to the corresponding tracker entry.
checklist.done: the filing calendar is updated with actual dates and confirmation status for every filing.

checklist.step: Escalate any filing at risk of missing its deadline
actions: Monitor the filing calendar for any package not locked at least 3 business days before its statutory or CMS deadline.
Escalate to the Controller and Head of Compliance the same day the at-risk status is identified.
Document the recovery plan and revised target date.
checklist.done: every at-risk filing has a documented escalation and recovery plan before its deadline.

checklist.step: File and calculate any late-filing penalty exposure

checklist.step: Confirm state-specific supplemental filing requirements are met

Log confirmation of each supplemental item's acceptance.
checklist.done: every state's supplemental filing requirement is submitted and confirmed.

checklist.step: Notify Records Management that submissions are complete for archival

Resolve any discrepancy between the transmittal log and the archive index before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: Records Management confirms receipt and archival of every submission in the period.

checklist.step: Report filing status to the Compliance Officer

File the summary in the compliance evidence repository.

checklist.step: Close out the filing cycle and reset the tracker for the next period

Load the next period's filing deadlines and reminder schedule into the tracker.

testing.step: Build the population of filings due in the test period

Resolve any missing deadline before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the filing tracker and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each filing to a captured confirmation

List unmatched or unconfirmed rows as automatic exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method

testing.step: Verify submission timeliness against the statutory deadline

Compare the timestamp to the statutory or CMS deadline (March 1 / May 15 / August 15 / November 15 / July 31 as applicable).
Flag any filing submitted after its deadline as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled filing's timeliness is independently verified against the correct deadline.

testing.step: Trace transmitted figures back to the filed source statement

Compare to the Controller's locked statement package for the same period.
Flag any figure that does not match.

testing.step: Test rejection and refiling handling on the sample

Confirm the corrected resubmission was accepted within 2 business days of the rejection.
Flag any refiling that exceeded the 2-business-day standard.
testing.done: every rejected sampled filing is confirmed refiled within 2 business days, or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Recompute any late-filing penalty exposure

Compare to the amount accrued by the Controller.
Flag any under- or over-accrual.
testing.done: recomputed penalty exposure matches the accrued amount, or the variance is logged.

testing.step: Confirm supplemental state filing items were submitted
actions: For sampled states with a supplemental cover letter or fee requirement, confirm the item was submitted and acknowledged.
Flag any missing supplemental item.
Confirm any required filing fee payment is evidenced in the state's acknowledgment.
testing.done: supplemental items are confirmed submitted for the sample, or missing items are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner, and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the state, filing type, and deadline missed.
Assign a root cause (data delay, system outage, missed reminder) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into the next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign, and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the compliance committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Assign an accountable owner to every calendar entry
actions: Confirm each calendar entry names the accountable team (Controller, Regulatory Reporting, Market Conduct Compliance, Product Compliance).
Fill any unassigned entry by consulting the ownerTeam mapping for the obligation type.
Circulate the ownership list for confirmation.
checklist.done: every calendar entry has a confirmed accountable owner.

checklist.step: Configure reminders for each calendar entry
actions: In the regulatory filing/issue tracker, set T-30/T-15/T-5 business-day reminders for each entry routed to its owning team's distribution list.
Test-fire a sample reminder to confirm delivery.
Log the reminder configuration date on the entry.
checklist.done: every calendar entry has configured, tested reminders routed to its owning team.

checklist.step: Link each filing to its timeliness evidence
actions: As each filing is submitted, attach the submission confirmation number and timestamp to its calendar entry.
Confirm the linked evidence file is retrievable from the transmittal log.
Flag any filing due date passed without linked evidence within 1 business day.
checklist.done: every completed filing's calendar entry carries linked, retrievable timeliness evidence.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the actual filing tracker weekly
actions: Compare open calendar entries to the statutory statement and MLR/MCAS transmittal logs weekly.
Update entry status (open, filed, late, extension granted) based on the comparison.
Escalate any discrepancy to the Regulatory Reporting Manager same week.
checklist.done: the calendar status is reconciled to the transmittal logs weekly with discrepancies escalated same week.

checklist.step: Publish the shared calendar view for stakeholders
actions: Mirror the master calendar to a SharePoint site accessible to Controller, Market Conduct Compliance, and Product Compliance.
Confirm the mirrored view refreshes automatically or on a defined schedule.
Set edit permissions limited to Regulatory Reporting.
checklist.done: the shared calendar view is published on SharePoint, refreshing correctly with edit access limited to Regulatory Reporting.

checklist.step: Review the calendar at each monthly compliance operations meeting
actions: Present the upcoming 60-day filing window at each monthly compliance operations meeting.
Confirm each owning team acknowledges its upcoming deadlines.
Log meeting attendance and acknowledgment.
checklist.done: the upcoming filing window is reviewed monthly with logged team acknowledgment.

checklist.step: Investigate and correct any missed reminder or stale entry
actions: Where a filing was late, determine whether the reminder fired and was received.
Correct the reminder configuration or routing if it failed.
Log the root cause and fix on the calendar entry's history.
checklist.done: every missed reminder is root-caused and the fix is logged on the entry.

checklist.step: Verify state deadline accuracy against a secondary source
actions: For SERFF-tracked deadlines, cross-check the calendar date against SERFF's Filing Rules page for the state.
For statutory statement/MLR/MCAS deadlines, cross-check against the NAIC filing calendar publication.
Correct any discrepancy found and log the correction.
checklist.done: every deadline is cross-checked against a secondary source with discrepancies corrected and logged.

checklist.step: Maintain a version history of calendar changes
actions: Enable change tracking on the master calendar file.
Confirm each date change, addition, or ownership reassignment is time-stamped with the editor's name.
Archive a version snapshot at each quarter-end.
checklist.done: calendar version history is tracked and a quarterly snapshot is archived.

checklist.step: Complete the annual calendar refresh certification by September 30
actions: Confirm every entry has been refreshed for the next filing year's confirmed dates.
Sign a completion certification memo.
File the memo in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed annual refresh certification is dated on or before September 30.

checklist.step: Escalate any state with an ambiguous or unpublished deadline
actions: Where a state has not published its current-year deadline, contact the state DOI filing desk for confirmation.
Log the inquiry and response, or use the prior year's deadline with a conservative buffer if unanswered.
Flag the entry for follow-up until confirmed.
checklist.done: every ambiguous deadline has a documented inquiry, response or conservative buffer, and a follow-up flag.

checklist.step: Archive the quarterly and annual calendar snapshots
actions: Save each quarterly snapshot and the annual refresh certification to the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the archive is indexed by filing year.
Verify the prior four quarterly snapshots remain retrievable before archiving the new one.
checklist.done: quarterly snapshots and the annual certification are archived and indexed by filing year.

checklist.step: Report calendar health to the Compliance Officer
actions: Summarize on-time filing rate, missed-reminder incidents, and open deadline-ambiguity items.
Present the summary at the next compliance committee meeting.
File the summary in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the calendar health summary is delivered to the Compliance Officer and committee.

testing.step: Build the population of calendar entries due in the test period
actions: Extract every calendar entry with a due date inside the test period from the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
Reconcile the extract count to the transmittal logs for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the transmittal logs and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each entry to an independently sourced deadline
actions: Independently pull each state's published filing deadline from the NAIC calendar or state DOI publication.
Compare to the date on the company's calendar entry.
List any mismatch as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row's date is independently verified, or a mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of MLR and audited-statement entries.
Take a random, seeded sample of 10 additional entries across states and filing types, minimum 20 total.
Record the seed, population size, and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-verify reminder configuration on the sample
actions: Open each sampled entry in the tracker and confirm T-30/T-15/T-5 reminders are configured and active.
Confirm the routing distribution list matches the accountable owning team.
Flag any entry with missing or misrouted reminders.
testing.done: reminder configuration and routing are independently verified for the sample.

testing.step: Trace timeliness evidence for each sampled entry
actions: Open the linked timeliness evidence (confirmation number, timestamp) for each sampled completed entry.
Compare the evidence date to the calendar due date to confirm on-time filing.
Flag any entry with missing or non-matching evidence.
testing.done: timeliness evidence is traced and confirmed for the sample, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Verify calendar ownership assignments
actions: Compare each sampled entry's assigned owning team to the ownerTeam mapping for that obligation type.
Flag any entry assigned to the wrong team.
Confirm the assigned owner's reminder distribution list is current.
testing.done: ownership assignments on the sample match the correct owning team, or mismatches are logged.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline math for entries with a computed due date
actions: For any entry whose due date is computed from a statutory period (e.g., deemer or review-period math), independently recompute the date.
Compare to the calendar entry.
Flag any miscalculation.
testing.done: computed due dates are independently recomputed and confirmed, or miscalculations are logged.

testing.step: Confirm the shared calendar view matches the master calendar
actions: Compare the SharePoint-published view to the master calendar for the sampled entries.
Flag any entry out of sync between the two.
Confirm the publish/refresh timestamp on SharePoint is current within the last refresh cycle.
testing.done: the published view matches the master calendar for the sample, or sync gaps are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner, and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the entry and the gap found.
Assign a root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign, and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 100%-accuracy threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the compliance committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Inventory every conduct area requiring a written procedure
actions: List every conduct-facing obligation under ACA/PHSA affecting Individual Health: CSR administration, EHB/limit prohibition, appeals handling, MLR rebate distribution.
Confirm each area has an assigned procedure owner and a current procedure document.
Flag any conduct area lacking a written procedure for immediate drafting.
checklist.done: every in-scope conduct area is inventoried with an assigned owner and either a current procedure or a flagged drafting gap.

checklist.step: Draft or update each procedure document
actions: For each conduct area, draft or revise the procedure describing the step-by-step process, roles, and systems used.
Insert the citation footer listing the current regulatory basis (45 CFR section and PHSA section).
Route the draft to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for content review.
checklist.done: each procedure document is drafted or updated with a current citation footer and routed for review.

checklist.step: Verify each citation footer against current regulatory text
actions: Re-read the current text of each cited 45 CFR section and PHSA section.
Confirm the citation still accurately supports the procedure's described conduct.
Flag and correct any stale or superseded citation.
checklist.done: every citation footer is confirmed current, or corrected where superseded.

checklist.step: Load procedures into the GRC platform with version control
actions: Upload each finalized procedure into the GRC platform's procedure library module.
Set the version number, owner, and next-review date fields.
Retire the prior version with a linked supersession note.
checklist.done: every procedure is loaded into the GRC platform with version control and a linked prior-version supersession note.

checklist.step: Obtain formal approval for each procedure
actions: Route each finalized procedure through the GRC platform's approval workflow to the Head of Compliance.
Confirm the approval is electronically signed and dated.
Publish the approved version to the procedure library.
checklist.done: every procedure carries a dated, electronically signed approval before publication.

checklist.step: Publish procedures to the operational teams that execute them
actions: Notify each executing team (Claims, Product Compliance, Regulatory Reporting) of the newly published or updated procedure.
Confirm the procedure is accessible from the team's working system or intranet link.
Log the publication date.
checklist.done: the executing teams are notified and confirmed to have access to the published procedure.

checklist.step: Train procedure owners and executing staff on material changes
actions: Identify any procedure change materially affecting how staff execute the process.
Deliver a briefing or job aid to the affected team summarizing the change.
Log attendance/acknowledgment of the briefing.
checklist.done: affected staff acknowledge training on every materially changed procedure.

checklist.step: Collect annual attestation from each procedure owner
actions: Send the annual attestation request through the GRC platform to each procedure owner.
Confirm the owner attests the procedure reflects current practice and citations.
Follow up on any unattested procedure within 5 business days of the request deadline.
checklist.done: every procedure owner's annual attestation is captured, with follow-up on any lapse within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Monitor for regulatory changes that trigger an out-of-cycle procedure update
actions: Monitor CMS and HHS bulletins for changes to CSR, EHB, or MLR rules affecting Individual Health.
Flag any change requiring an immediate procedure update rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager same week.
checklist.done: regulatory changes are monitored and any triggering update is flagged and communicated same week.

checklist.step: Perform the out-of-cycle update when triggered
actions: Revise the affected procedure per the flagged regulatory change.
Route through the same citation-verification and approval workflow as the annual cycle.
Publish and notify affected teams within 10 business days of the trigger.
checklist.done: any triggered out-of-cycle update is published and communicated within 10 business days of the trigger.

checklist.step: Reconcile the procedure library against the conduct-area inventory
actions: Compare the published procedure library to the conduct-area inventory built in step 1.
Confirm every inventoried area has a current, approved procedure.
Flag and remediate any gap.
checklist.done: every inventoried conduct area has a current, approved procedure, or the gap is remediated.

checklist.step: Complete the annual review cycle by September 30
actions: Confirm every procedure has been reviewed, re-cited, and re-approved within the past 12 months.
Sign a completion certification memo listing any residual open item.
File the memo in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed annual review completion certification is dated on or before September 30.

checklist.step: Log procedure exceptions and drive remediation
actions: Log any procedure found stale, miscited, or unapproved as a tracker exception with root cause and owner.
Set a remediation due date and monitor to closure.
Escalate any remediation open past 30 days to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every procedure exception has a logged root cause, owner, and remediation date, with escalation past 30 days.

checklist.step: Archive superseded procedure versions
actions: Move each superseded procedure version to the compliance evidence repository with its supersession date.
Confirm the archive preserves the full version history for exam purposes.
Verify the current published version links back to its full supersession chain.
checklist.done: superseded versions are archived with supersession dates and full version history preserved.

checklist.step: Report procedure library health to the compliance committee
actions: Summarize review completion rate, open exceptions, and out-of-cycle updates for the year.
Present the summary at the next compliance committee meeting.
File the summary in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the procedure library health summary is delivered to the compliance committee.

testing.step: Build the population of procedures required to be current
actions: Extract the full procedure library and version metadata from the GRC platform.
Independently build the required conduct-area list from the ACA/PHSA obligations affecting Individual Health.
Compare the two lists and log any conduct area without a corresponding procedure.
testing.done: the procedure population is reconciled to the independently built conduct-area list.

testing.step: Reconcile review dates to the 12-month standard
actions: Pull the last-reviewed date for every procedure in the library.
Flag any procedure not reviewed within the trailing 12 months as an automatic exception.
Compute the percentage of procedures within the 12-month standard for the workpaper summary.
testing.done: every procedure's review date is checked against the 12-month standard, with lapses logged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of procedures covering CSR administration and MLR rebate handling.
Take a random, seeded sample of 5 additional procedures from the remaining library, minimum 10 total.
Record the seed, population size, and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-verify the citation footer for each sampled procedure
actions: Independently re-read the current text of each cited 45 CFR/PHSA section for the sampled procedures.
Confirm the citation still accurately supports the described conduct without looking at the prior verification note first.
Log any citation now stale or incorrect.
testing.done: each sampled procedure's citation is independently re-verified, with stale citations logged.

testing.step: Confirm approval and version control on the sample
actions: Confirm each sampled procedure carries a dated, signed Head of Compliance approval in the GRC platform.
Confirm the version history shows the prior version properly retired and linked.
Flag any missing approval or broken version linkage.
testing.done: approval and version control are confirmed for the sample, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Test procedure content against actual operational practice
actions: Interview the executing team for each sampled procedure and observe or walk through the actual process.
Compare the observed practice to the documented procedure steps.
Flag any material deviation between practice and documentation.
testing.done: documented procedure content is confirmed to match observed operational practice for the sample, or deviations are logged.

testing.step: Confirm attestation completeness for the sample
actions: Confirm each sampled procedure's owner submitted the current-year attestation in the GRC platform.
Flag any missing or overdue attestation.
Confirm the attestation date is on or after the procedure's last-reviewed date.
testing.done: attestation completeness is confirmed for the sample, or missing attestations are logged.

testing.step: Test that any recent regulatory change is reflected
actions: Identify any CMS/HHS bulletin issued in the test period affecting CSR, EHB, or MLR rules.
Confirm the relevant procedure was updated within 10 business days of the bulletin per the out-of-cycle standard.
Flag any procedure not updated timely.
testing.done: recent regulatory changes are confirmed reflected in the affected procedures within the standard, or lapses are logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner, and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the procedure and the gap found.
Assign a root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign, and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 100%-currency threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the compliance committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance and Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; reviewed annually against the current MCAS data-call specification

checklist.step: Pull the current-year MCAS Health data-call specification
actions: In the NAIC MCAS system, download the current-year Health interrogatory specification and submission guide.
Compare against the prior year's specification and flag any new or changed interrogatory.
Circulate the changed interrogatories to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the current specification is downloaded with changes from the prior year flagged and circulated.

checklist.step: Map each interrogatory to its source data system
actions: For each interrogatory (claims processing time, denial/appeal counts, complaint counts, network adequacy metrics), identify the owning source system (Claims Platform, complaints tracker, provider network system).
Document the extraction query or report used for each interrogatory in a mapping workbook.
Confirm the mapping workbook covers 100% of the current specification's interrogatories.
checklist.done: the mapping workbook covers every current-year interrogatory with a documented source and extraction method.

checklist.step: Extract claims-processing data elements
actions: In the Claims Platform run the claims-timeliness and claims-denial report for the Individual Health block for the reporting year.
Export claim counts by processing-time band and denial reason code as specified by the interrogatory definitions.
Save the export to the MCAS compilation workbook.
checklist.done: claims-processing data elements are extracted and saved to the compilation workbook per the interrogatory definitions.

checklist.step: Extract complaint and grievance/appeal data elements
actions: Pull the complaint log for the Individual Health block for the reporting year, categorized by complaint type per the MCAS definitions.
Pull grievance and internal/external appeal counts and outcomes for the same period.
Hand the extract to Regulatory Reporting Analyst for compilation.
checklist.done: complaint and grievance/appeal data elements are extracted, categorized per MCAS definitions, and handed off.

checklist.step: Extract underwriting, marketing, and network-adequacy data elements
actions: Pull new-business and renewal underwriting counts, marketing/advertising material counts, and network-adequacy metrics from their respective source systems.
Map each to its corresponding MCAS interrogatory line.
Save to the compilation workbook.
checklist.done: underwriting, marketing, and network-adequacy data elements are extracted, mapped, and saved.

checklist.step: Reconcile MLR and risk-adjustment data feeding shared interrogatories
actions: Where an MCAS interrogatory overlaps with ACA MLR annual report or risk-adjustment (45 CFR 153.610/153.700-153.740) data, pull the corresponding figure from the MLR/risk-adjustment workpapers.
Reconcile the two sources and resolve any variance before compiling the MCAS submission.
Document the reconciliation in the compilation workbook.
checklist.done: shared MLR/risk-adjustment data elements reconcile to their MCAS interrogatory counterparts with the reconciliation documented.

checklist.step: Compile the full MCAS submission file
actions: Consolidate all extracted and reconciled data elements into the NAIC MCAS submission file format.
Confirm every required interrogatory field is populated with no blanks.
Save the compiled file to the compilation workbook version history.
checklist.done: the compiled MCAS submission file has every required field populated with no blanks.

checklist.step: Run the NAIC MCAS system's validation check
actions: Upload the compiled file to the NAIC MCAS online system's validation/staging area.
Run the built-in edit checks and review every flagged warning or error.
Correct the underlying data and re-run validation until clean.
checklist.done: the MCAS validation check runs clean with every flagged item corrected.

checklist.step: Obtain Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager review and sign-off
actions: Review the validated submission for reasonableness against the prior year's filed MCAS data.
Confirm any year-over-year swing greater than 20% on a key interrogatory is explained.
Sign off on the submission for release.
checklist.done: the submission is reviewed for reasonableness, material swings are explained, and sign-off is recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the MCAS Health data call to the NAIC
actions: In the NAIC MCAS system, select the company code, reporting year, and the Health line of business.
Submit the validated, signed-off file through the MCAS submission gateway.
Capture the NAIC MCAS confirmation receipt with submission date and time.
checklist.done: the MCAS submission is transmitted with a captured NAIC confirmation receipt.

checklist.step: Monitor for NAIC data-quality follow-up requests
actions: Check the NAIC MCAS system for any post-submission data-quality query for 10 business days after submission.
Route any query to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager same-day.
Prepare and submit the requested clarification or correction within the NAIC's stated response window.
checklist.done: the 10-business-day monitoring window is completed and any NAIC query is answered within its response window.

checklist.step: Update the filing tracker with the submission outcome
actions: Enter the submission date, confirmation number, and validation status into the filing tracker.
Flag if the submission occurred within 5 business days of the NAIC deadline for root-cause review.
Attach the NAIC confirmation receipt to the tracker entry.
checklist.done: the filing tracker is updated with the submission outcome and any near-deadline filing is flagged.

checklist.step: Archive the MCAS submission package
actions: Save the compiled submission file, interrogatory mapping workbook, validation log, and NAIC confirmation to the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the archive is indexed by reporting year.
Apply the 10-year retention label to the archived package.
checklist.done: the MCAS submission package is archived and indexed by reporting year.

checklist.step: Debrief the submission cycle and update the interrogatory mapping
actions: Hold a post-submission debrief noting any interrogatory-mapping difficulty or data-quality issue encountered.
Update the mapping workbook and procedure ahead of next year's specification release.
Circulate the updated mapping workbook to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst for next cycle's kickoff.
checklist.done: the debrief is held and the mapping workbook/procedure is updated for the next cycle.

checklist.step: Report MCAS submission status to the Compliance Officer
actions: Summarize submission timeliness, validation issues, and any NAIC follow-up for the cycle.
Present the summary at the next compliance committee meeting.
File the summary in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the MCAS submission status summary is delivered to the Compliance Officer and committee.

testing.step: Build the population of interrogatory data elements submitted
actions: Pull the full submitted MCAS Health interrogatory file from the NAIC MCAS system for the test period.
Reconcile the element count to the current-year specification's required interrogatory count.
Resolve any missing interrogatory before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the required interrogatory count and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the submission to the compilation workbook
actions: Match each submitted interrogatory value to its corresponding row in the compilation workbook.
List any unmatched or altered value as an automatic exception.
Record the match rate in the workpaper before proceeding to sampling.
testing.done: every submitted value is matched to the compilation workbook or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of interrogatories shared with the MLR annual report and risk-adjustment data.
Take a random, seeded sample of 10 additional interrogatories, minimum 20 total.
Record the seed, population size, and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and documented in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the extraction for each sampled interrogatory
actions: Independently re-run the source-system query (Claims Platform, complaints tracker, network system) for each sampled interrogatory.
Compare the independently extracted value to the submitted value within the 1% tolerance.
Log any value outside tolerance as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled interrogatory is independently re-extracted and compared within tolerance, with exceptions logged.

testing.step: Test the MLR/risk-adjustment reconciliation on the sample
actions: For each sampled shared interrogatory, compare the MCAS value to the corresponding MLR annual report or risk-adjustment workpaper figure.
Confirm the documented reconciliation explains any difference.
Flag any unreconciled difference.
testing.done: MLR/risk-adjustment reconciliation is independently confirmed for the sample, or unreconciled differences are logged.

testing.step: Verify the NAIC validation log shows a clean pass
actions: Pull the NAIC MCAS system's validation/edit-check log for the submission.
Confirm no unresolved warning or error remains against the submitted file.
Flag any unresolved validation item.
testing.done: the validation log shows a clean pass, or unresolved items are logged.

testing.step: Recompute submission timeliness against the NAIC deadline
actions: Compare the captured NAIC confirmation timestamp to the published MCAS filing deadline for the reporting year.
Flag the submission as late if the timestamp is after the deadline.
Confirm any late submission has a documented root cause and remediation entry.
testing.done: submission timeliness is independently verified against the published deadline.

testing.step: Confirm any NAIC data-quality follow-up was resolved
actions: Check the NAIC MCAS system and filing tracker for any post-submission data-quality query.
Confirm the response was submitted within the NAIC's stated response window.
Flag any unresolved or late-answered query.
testing.done: any NAIC follow-up query is confirmed resolved within its response window, or the lapse is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner, and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the interrogatory and the variance or gap found.
Assign a root cause (extraction error, mapping error, source-system change) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign, and report the test
